nodes.name: 01:00 LA — full run
nodes.notes: Anchored to the AD ACCOUNT's clock, not yours. act_153704749222533 is America/Los_Angeles and a day closes at midnight there, so 01:00 PT is the first moment yesterday is complete. Set the WORKFLOW timezone to America/Los_Angeles (Settings > Timezone) or this fires at the wrong hour.

nodes.name: 13:00 LA — numbers only
nodes.notes: Halves the staleness. With one nightly run, a question asked at 5pm is answered from data up to 17 hours old, and 'spend is down' can mean 'the morning has not been imported'.

nodes.name: Import both phases, then suggest
nodes.notes:
Both phases AND the creative suggestion — sync.py chains scripts/suggest.py after a successful import, so this is the whole pipeline in one command. It takes minutes: structure crawls the ad list, insights pulls ~4 days, then one model call of about 45 seconds.

onError is continueRegularOutput on purpose: exit 2 means a run was already going, which is the lock working, not a failure. Branching happens in the next node.

parameters.command: cd /d "C:\Users\Renegade\Desktop\Ads Growth Engine" && ".venv\Scripts\python.exe" scripts\sync.py --brand renegade --phase insights --no-suggest

nodes.name: Import insights only
nodes.notes:
Insights only, and no suggestion. ~80 seconds, one Graph request over a ~4-day window.

Structure is skipped because the ad list changes slowly and the crawl is the expensive half. --no-suggest keeps this to one model call a day: the 01:00 run already published one, and a second would cost ~$0.37 to say much the same thing.

nodes.name: Did the import fail?
nodes.notes:
ONLY exit 1 is a failure worth waking somebody for.

  0  everything pulled
  1  something failed — read logs\sync.log
  2  a sync was already running, so this one did nothing

Alerting on 2 trains people to ignore the alert: it is the lock refusing to let two pulls race the Meta rate limiter, which is the lock doing its job. A suggestion that failed after a successful import also does not reach here — sync.py logs it and leaves the exit code alone, because the import either happened or it did not and that is what this branch is asking.

nodes.name: Did the midday pull fail?
nodes.notes: Same three exit codes as the morning run.

nodes.name: ALERT — wire your channel here
nodes.notes:
Replace this with Slack / email / whatever you use. Deliberately left as a No-Op rather than guessed at.

Useful fields on the incoming item:
  {{ $json.exitCode }}   1
  {{ $json.stderr }}     the one-sentence reason
  {{ $json.stdout }}     the same lines that went to logs\sync.log

What a failure usually means, in rough order of likelihood:
  • the Meta token expired — a System User token is silent when it dies
  • an ad account the token cannot read is still marked active
  • the Supabase pooler dropped the connection mid-write

`python -m intel status --brand renegade` names all three in one sentence each.

nodes.name: Quiet — imported, or already running
nodes.notes: Exit 0 or 2. Nothing to do: the dashboard's import card already shows when the last pull landed, and /suggestions already carries what was published from it.

nodes.name: ALERT — midday
nodes.notes: Wire to the same channel as the morning alert.
